answer: Sealed Challenge Vault. Each identity must publish a fresh, randomly seeded cryptographic puzzle whose solution is verifiable but not reusable, plus a signed atlas of prior solutions it has consumed. A new identity is admitted only if its puzzle is unspent and its atlas references no overlapping puzzle lineage. Attackers pay a per-identity cost of solving one unique puzzle and maintaining an island of isolated solution history that cannot be merged, so mass registration scales linearly in compute and bookkeeping rather than amortizing.
